messages:
customer-prod: Hey team — starting ~08:50 UTC we started seeing intermittent 502 / TLS handshake failures from our private VPC in eu-west-1 when calling the private Redwood API (private.redwood.internal). Only some AZs in eu-west-1 are affected. Happening across multiple hosts in our autoscaling group. Repro steps below.

customer-prod: Repro (short):
```
curl -v https://private.redwood.internal/v1/health -H "Host: private.redwood.internal"
* About to connect() to 10.11.22.45 port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake: error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number
```

jessica.support: Thanks — sorry about the hit. Can you paste the output of `dig +short private.redwood.internal @<your-resolver>` from two different AZs (one that works, one that fails)? Also please run `openssl s_client -connect <IP>:443 -servername private.redwood.internal -showcerts` against any IP that fails. We'll triage. Ticket SUP-2345 opened.

customer-prod: dig results (eu-west-1a vs eu-west-1c):
```
# eu-west-1a (failing)
10.11.22.45
# eu-west-1c (working)
10.12.33.66
```
traceroute (redacted): shows hop to 10.11.22.45 then no response after LB.

customer-prod: openssl s_client against 10.11.22.45 shows cert subject CN=internal-gateway.redwood.net (not private.redwood.internal) and validation errors.

tyler.sre: Looking. Two quick hypotheses: 1) split-horizon DNS (different resolver configs in AZs) pointing to different load balancer pools, and one pool has misconfigured SNI/cert; 2) NAT / egress path causing requests to hit a different front than intended.

maria-network: Also check that your VPC egress ACL / firewall allowlist hasn't been tightened recently — if the egress is SNATting from different IP blocks per AZ you might hit region-scoped allowlist rules on our side. Can you paste the NAT IP ranges for the failing AZ?

customer-prod: NAT egress IP (eu-west-1a): 52.214.77.129
NAT egress IP (eu-west-1c): 18.203.12.5

devops-bot: AUTO: matched NAT ips 52.214.77.129 -> eu-west-1a, 18.203.12.5 -> eu-west-1c. Noted.

tyler.sre: Confirmed from our side: requests from 52.214.77.129 are hitting a canary pool in us-west-2 that had an incorrect listener SNI mapping (internal-gateway cert). That explains CN mismatch and TLS handshake failing. The weird part: why only some AZs in eu-west are getting that pool — DNS.

tyler.sre: I pulled resolver traces and see that eu-west-1a's resolver still returns a cached A record (10.11.22.45) that maps to the canary LB. The canary LB was recently deployed for a subset of client IP ranges while we validate a new edge config. TTL for that split-view entry was high and some resolvers haven't expired yet.

jessica.support: Action plan: 1) temporary workaround — add host entry on affected hosts pointing private.redwood.internal -> 10.12.33.66 (working IP) or add the NAT IP 52.214.77.129 to your egress allowlist to be routed to standard pool (if easier). 2) We'll roll back the canary listener mapping and reissue a cert for the canary immediately. 3) lower the split-horizon TTL and flush caches.

customer-prod: We added a host entry on a test instance and `curl` now returns 200. Workaround confirmed. If you can fix on your side we'll remove hosts entry.

eng-runtime: We're escalating to runtime infra — will roll back listener changes in us-west-2 and rebind correct cert. Also pushing a small DNS TTL override to 30s for the split view so caches expire quickly.

maria-network: On your side, once we flip, please `sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches` or restart the resolver on instance. Also check any local DNS caching (nscd/dnsmasq).

tyler.sre: Rollback performed at 1792003602. Listener mapping reverted, cert re-bound. Lowered split-horizon TTL to 30s.

devops-bot: NOTIFY: rollout completed by eng-runtime at 1792003609.

customer-prod: Flushed DNS and retested — all hosts in eu-west-1 are now resolving to the correct IPs and `curl` returns 200. No more TLS errors.

jessica.support: Great — closing the loop. Root cause: canary LB listener misconfiguration + stale split-horizon DNS TTL causing cross-AZ inconsistency. Remediation: rebind cert, rollback canary, lowered TTL, recommend you remove the host entry after 15m and monitor. We'll follow up with a postmortem and a note to reduce TTLs during canary deploys.

customer-prod: Thanks everyone — confirmed healthy for 30+ minutes. Appreciate the quick turnaround :thumbsup:

tyler.sre: Filed follow-up: ENG-INC-981 — add automation to check split-horizon consistency across resolvers before canary LB routing changes.

jessica.support: Marking SUP-2345 RESOLVED. If anything reappears ping this thread and we'll reopen.
